author: Hyoungseo Son
gitActivitySummary:
4 commits on feature/notifications (Boston session)

  feat: add Notification model + DB schema
      lib/notifications/model.ts, prisma/schema.prisma
  feat: deliver notifications over a WebSocket channel
      lib/ws.ts, app/api/notifications/route.ts
  wip: notification preferences endpoint (GET only)
      app/api/notifications/preferences/route.ts
  fix: re-open the socket after a dropped connection
      lib/ws.ts

scenarios.situation: The preferences POST endpoint writes the request body straight to the database with no validation. A malformed request — missing the `channels` array, or a bad `mutedUntil` date — throws and returns a 500.
scenarios.suggestedApproach: Validate before saving: check that `channels` is a non-empty array of known values, and that `mutedUntil` parses as a date. The GET handler right above it shows the exact shape I expect. I left a `// TODO: validate` comment on the spot.

scenarios.situation: The WebSocket connection authenticates with a placeholder header check (`x-temp-token`). It works on my machine, but it is not real auth — anyone could open a socket.
scenarios.suggestedApproach: Swap it for `getSession()` from lib/auth.ts — the REST routes already use that exact pattern. I marked it with `// TODO: real auth` in lib/ws.ts. This one has to be done before we demo — it's a security hole.

scenarios.situation: There is an 'Unsubscribe' button in the UI, but it does nothing — the endpoint behind it was never built. I ran out of time.
scenarios.suggestedApproach: Add `DELETE /api/notifications/subscription` that sets `active = false` on the row. The Notification model already has the `active` field, so it is a small change. The button already fires the request — it just 404s right now.

scenarios.situation: Reconnect works, but after a dropped connection it fires the 'connected' event twice, so the user briefly sees a duplicate toast.
scenarios.suggestedApproach: Guard the connect handler with a `hasConnected` ref, or debounce it. I hit this late and didn't fix it — it's cosmetic, so it's the lowest priority of the four.

metadata.developerNotes: Notifications are about 70% there. The model, the WebSocket delivery, and the reconnect logic are solid — I tested those by hand. What is NOT done: the preferences endpoint only has GET (POST has no validation and will crash on bad input), the WebSocket auth is a temporary hack, and the whole unsubscribe flow is missing. If you only have time for one thing, do the WebSocket auth (scenario 2) — it's a security hole and we can't demo with it. Everything I touched is on the `feature/notifications` branch. Ask the stand-in if anything is unclear — I tried to leave enough context. Good luck, talk soon.
